title: What The Taiko Knows — EN/JA/ZH (Chas McIvor)
style: jazz lounge piano bar dry wit spoken word observational 108bpm upright bass brushed snare deadpan baritone male vocal Japanese Chinese philosophy language learning thunder
lyrics:
[Verse 1 — English]
The taiko drum is not a subtle instrument
It is a barrel the size of a small car with intent
You don't tap a taiko — you address it from the shoulder
Every note a statement and the statement gets no older

[Verse 2 — Japanese, with English translation]
太鼓は知っている、体が言葉になることを
[The taiko knows that the body becomes words]
打つたびに、天地が揺れる音がする
[With every strike, a sound of heaven and earth shaking]
二本のバチが空気を切り、魂を呼ぶ
[Two bachi sticks cut the air, calling the soul]
太鼓が知っていることを、私は全身で感じる
[What the taiko knows, I feel with my whole body]

[Chorus — English]
What does the taiko know that I don't know?
It knows that some truths need to land with the force of a blow
What does the taiko know in an open field?
It knows that thunder was the original percussion revealed
That's my boy

[Bridge — Chinese Mandarin, with English translation]
太鼓的声音像雷，震撼大地和天空
[The taiko's sound is like thunder, shaking earth and sky]
每一击都是宣言，每一声都是力量
[Every strike is a declaration, every sound is power]
古代的战士用太鼓传递信息
[Ancient warriors used the taiko to send messages]
太鼓知道，身体就是乐器
[The taiko knows, the body itself is the instrument]

[Outro — All three languages]
What the taiko knows… 太鼓が知ること… 太鼓知道的
Thunder was first — 雷が最初だった — 雷声是第一
That's my boy
